design.title: DeceptiWAF — Deception-Based Web Application Firewall
design.reference: Linear.app marketing deck meets Notion product pages — soft pastel gradients, solid white cards, generous whitespace, violet/pink accents

slides.title: Cover — DeceptiWAF
slides.task_brief:
COVER SLIDE. Centered layout on the pastel gradient background.

Top: a small pill badge 'CYBERSECURITY PROJECT · 2025' in violet.

Center: Massive headline 'DeceptiWAF' in gradient text (violet → pink), font-size ~88px, Plus Jakarta Sans ExtraBold. Below it, subtitle in 28px slate: 'A Deception-Based Web Application Firewall with Brute-Force Honeypot'.

Below subtitle: a row of 3 small tech pills: 'Node.js', 'Express', 'Socket.io' — each white pill with violet text.

Bottom-center: credit line 'Kalyani University · Software Engineering Project' in 14px slate-500.

Top-right corner: a subtle shield icon (Material Icons 'security') in a soft violet circle, 48px.

No image needed. Pure typographic cover.

Speaker notes: full script (~100 words) introducing the project — what DeceptiWAF is, why we built it, the core deception concept, and what the audience will see in the next 10 slides.

slides.title: The Problem
slides.task_brief:
SPLIT LAYOUT: left 55% text, right 45% stat cards.

Left side:
- Small pill 'THE PROBLEM' in rose.
- H1 headline (36px): 'Web apps face relentless automated attacks'
- 3 bullet points (16px, slate-600, each with a small Material Icon):
  1. icon 'bug_report' — 'SQL injection, XSS, and path traversal target every web form'
  2. icon 'lock_open' — 'Brute-force login attacks are automated, parallel, and cheap to run'
  3. icon 'visibility_off' — 'Traditional WAFs block-and-forget — they never learn who the attacker is'

Right side: 3 stacked stat cards (white, rounded-2xl, soft shadow):
- Card 1: big number '83%' in violet (JetBrains Mono, 44px), label 'of web apps have vulnerabilities (OWASP)'
- Card 2: big number '#1' in pink (44px), label 'SQL injection in web attack rankings'
- Card 3: big number '177' in amber (44px), label 'avg days to detect a breach (IBM)'

Speaker notes: full script (~120 words) explaining the threat landscape — why web apps are attacked, why block-and-forget isn't enough, and the gap DeceptiWAF fills.

slides.title: Our Approach — Deception
slides.task_brief:
KEY MESSAGE SLIDE. Centered, bold, minimal.

Top: small pill 'OUR APPROACH' in violet.

Center: massive statement (48px, Plus Jakarta Sans Bold, slate-800):
'Don't just block attackers —'
next line in gradient text (violet → pink):
'trap them.'

Below: subtext (20px, slate-600, max-width 800px, centered):
'DeceptiWAF combines a scoring WAF with a deception honeypot. Instead of rejecting brute-forcers with a 401, we lie "Login Successful" and serve a fake dashboard — then watch every move they make on the SOC feed.'

Bottom: 3 horizontal pills with icons:
- '🛡 WAF blocks' (rose pill)
- '🕸 Honeypot traps' (fuchsia pill)
- '👁 SOC watches' (violet pill)

Speaker notes: full script (~130 words) explaining the deception philosophy — why trapping is better than blocking, what attackers see, how the SOC benefits.

slides.title: Architecture Overview
slides.task_brief:
BENTO GRID: 2x2 white cards, each a module. Title above grid: 'Architecture' (32px, gradient text).

Card 1 (top-left): icon 'web' in violet circle. Title 'Module 1 — Target App'. Body: 'Express server mimicking KLY University portal. Login page, student dashboard, course search — the decoy surface attackers hit.'

Card 2 (top-right): icon 'shield' in rose circle. Title 'Module 2 — WAF Middleware'. Body: '50+ regex rules across SQLi/XSS/PathTraversal/MaliciousUAs. Scoring engine blocks at score > 4. Multi-layer de-obfuscation pipeline.'

Card 3 (bottom-left): icon 'bug_report' in fuchsia circle. Title 'Module 3 — CredShield Honeypot'. Body: 'Tracks failed logins per IP. After 3 fails, honeypot arms. 4th attempt is "successful" — serves fake dashboard with deterministic fake profile.'

Card 4 (bottom-right): icon 'monitoring' in emerald circle. Title 'Module 4 — SOC Dashboard'. Body: 'Real-time Socket.io feed, IP geolocation via ip-api.com, event history (last 500), top attackers catalog, admin APIs.'

Center overlay between cards: a small pill 'Socket.io event bus' in slate, indicating modules communicate via Socket.io.

Speaker notes: full script (~140 words) walking through each module and how they connect.

slides.title: WAF Engine — Scoring + De-obfuscation
slides.task_brief:
SPLIT: left 50% explanation, right 50% pipeline.

Left:
- Pill 'MODULE 2 · WAF ENGINE' in rose.
- H2 (28px): 'Scoring engine, not hard blocks'
- Body (15px slate-600): 'Each regex rule has a point value. The request score is the sum of all matched rules. Block threshold = 4. This lets benign traffic with a single low-score indicator (like a -- in a legitimate comment) pass through, while real attacks trigger multiple high-score rules.'
- Example table (mono font, compact):
  | Payload | Rules hit | Score | Result |
  | UNION SELECT | sqli_union_select (4) | 4 | ✗ flagged |
  | ' UNION SELECT 1,2,3 -- | union(4) + comment(1) | 5 | ✓ BLOCKED |

Right: 'De-obfuscation pipeline' heading, then a vertical stack of chips (each a white card with mono text, connected by small down-arrows):
1. 'Raw input' (slate)
2. 'decodeURIComponent × 3' (violet) — catches %27, %2527
3. 'decodeHtmlEntities' (violet) — catches < < <
4. 'normalize("NFKC")' (violet) — catches ＵＮＩＯＮ
5. 'strip /* comments */' (violet) — catches UNION/**/SELECT
6. 'Pattern match (50+ rules)' (pink, bold) — final detection

Bottom-right callout: '50+ rules · 4 attack families · 8 evasion techniques defeated'

Speaker notes: full script (~150 words) explaining scoring rationale + the multi-layer pipeline.

slides.title: CredShield — The Honeypot
slides.task_brief:
HORIZONTAL TIMELINE: 5 steps left-to-right. Title above: 'CredShield — Brute-Force Honeypot' (32px gradient text).

Timeline is a horizontal line with 5 circular nodes. Each node has a number, a label below, and a color:
1. Node 1 (amber): 'Attempt 1' / 'Failed login' / 'count=1'
2. Node 2 (amber): 'Attempt 2' / 'Failed login' / 'count=2'
3. Node 3 (orange): 'Attempt 3' / 'HONEYPOT ARMED' / 'threshold crossed'
4. Node 4 (fuchsia): 'Attempt 4' / '"Login Successful"' / 'TRAP SPRINGS'
5. Node 5 (violet): 'Attacker lands on /dashboard' / 'served fake profile' / 'silent deception'

Below the timeline: two callout cards side-by-side:
- Card A (left): icon 'fingerprint' — 'Deterministic fake profiles: same username = same fake student, every time. No real user data exposed.'
- Card B (right): icon 'schedule' — 'Auto-disarms after 30 min of inactivity. Legit users on shared IPs aren't locked out forever.'

Speaker notes: full script (~140 words) walking through the trap flow + why deterministic profiles matter.

slides.title: SOC Dashboard — Live Command Center
slides.task_brief:
SPLIT: left 45% feature list, right 55% mockup.

Left:
- Pill 'MODULE 4 · SOC DASHBOARD' in emerald.
- H2 (28px): 'Real-time attack visibility'
- 5 bullet points (15px slate-600, each with a small colored dot):
  • 🟢 Live WAF block feed via Socket.io — IP, attack type, score, payload, hit breakdown
  • 🟣 Purple honeypot trap alerts with fake identity served + attacker fingerprint
  • 🌍 IP geolocation via ip-api.com — city, country, ISP, flag emoji
  • 📊 Top attackers catalog + trapped attackers panel with admin reset
  • 🔌 Admin APIs: /api/stats, /api/events/recent, /api/honeypot/reset

Right: a dark panel mockup (bg #1e1932, rounded-2xl, padding 20px) simulating the live feed. Mono font, 12px, 5 example lines:
  [14:23:01] [BLOCK] SQLi score=5/4 ip=10.0.0.7 🇺🇸 Ashburn, US
    - sqli_or_tautology (4pt) [body.studentId]
  [14:23:08] [BRUTE] ip=203.0.113.9 user=admin fails=2/3
  [14:23:15] [HONEYPOT ARMED] ip=203.0.113.9 after 3 fails
  [14:23:22] [HONEYPOT TRAP] ip=203.0.113.9 served_fake=Dev Raina

Below mockup: tiny label 'Dark feed panel · real Socket.io events'.

Speaker notes: full script (~140 words) describing what admins see + how geo + fingerprinting help attribution.

slides.title: Anti-Evasion — Catching the Sneaky Stuff
slides.task_brief:
COMPARISON TABLE. Title: 'Anti-Evasion — Phase 5' (32px gradient text). Subtitle: 'Multi-layer de-obfuscation catches what single-pass WAFs miss.'

Two-column table (white card, rounded-2xl, full width):
- Header row: 'Naïve WAF (single-pass)' | 'DeceptiWAF (multi-layer)'
- Row 1: '<script> (HTML entities)' | '✓ blocked — decodeHtmlEntities'
- Row 2: 'ＵＮＩＯＮ (full-width Unicode)' | '✓ blocked — normalize NFKC'
- Row 3: 'UNION/**/SELECT (SQL comment)' | '✓ blocked — strip /* */'
- Row 4: '%2527 OR 1=1 (double URL-encoded)' | '✓ blocked — recursive decode'
- Row 5: 'UNION     SELECT (whitespace pad)' | '✓ blocked — collapse whitespace'

Left column cells: rose-50 background, mono font, ✗ icon. Right column cells: emerald-50 background, mono font, ✓ icon.

Bottom callout pill (centered): '8 evasion techniques defeated · 28/28 tests passing'

Speaker notes: full script (~130 words) explaining why each evasion works against naïve WAFs and how the multi-layer pipeline defeats them.
